title: Why is August named after a Roman emperor?

post.caption: Ancient Rome, episode 7: Octavian beats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium, becomes Augustus in 27 BC, renames a month and turns a city of brick into marble. Images: public domain / CC0 (Castro, Vatican statue, The Met, Rijksmuseum, NAM Athens), AI illustrations marked. Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Every summer, you write this man's name without knowing it.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why is August named after a Roman emperor?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Because of Augustus, Rome's first emperor. He entered politics at eighteen, and ended up ruling Rome for forty years.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who was he?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Julius Caesar's great-nephew, Octavian. In his will, Caesar adopted him as his son and heir.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How did he win power?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: By defeating his rival Mark Antony and the queen of Egypt, Cleopatra. In 31 BC, their fleets met his at Actium, off the coast of Greece.
beats.say: By defeating his rival Mark Antony and the queen of Egypt, Cleopatra. In thirty-one BC, their fleets met his at Actium, off the coast of Greece.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Octavian's admiral Agrippa won. Antony and Cleopatra fled to Egypt, and a year later both took their own lives.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And then?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Egypt became his. Rome's civil wars were over, and Octavian was the most powerful man in the world.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did he make himself king?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Never openly. He said he had restored the Republic, and called himself only the first citizen. But in 27 BC, the Senate gave him a new name: Augustus, the revered one.
beats.say: Never openly. He said he had restored the Republic, and called himself only the first citizen. But in twenty-seven BC, the Senate gave him a new name: Augustus, the revered one.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And the month?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 8 BC, the month Sextilis was renamed August, because his greatest victories, like taking Egypt, happened in it.
beats.say: In eight BC, the month Sextilis was renamed August, because his greatest victories, like taking Egypt, happened in it.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did he steal a day from February to make August longer?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: No, that's a myth from the Middle Ages. August already had thirty-one days.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: What did he do with Rome itself?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: He rebuilt it. He boasted that he found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble. His reign began two centuries of peace, the Pax Romana.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How did he die?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Peacefully, in August AD 14, aged seventy-five. His last words, it's said, were: if I played my part well, applaud.
beats.say: Peacefully, in August, A D fourteen, aged seventy-five. His last words, it's said, were: if I played my part well, applaud.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Like the video and follow History Sketches for the next episode: Roman concrete.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments: who was the greater Roman, Caesar or Augustus?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Two thousand years later, his name still comes back every summer.
